edition.note: the at-home first stage of the full Core, same item ids

intro.lead: This is the first step of The Core: the prep. You fill it in at home, on your own, at your pace. Everything you write here goes straight into The Core, so in the studio we skip the basics and get to the decisions that matter.
promise: About 51 minutes, an hour at most. Each module tells you how long it takes.
We save as you go, on this device and on our side. Close it any time and pick up where you left off, from the same link.
There are no wrong answers. If something stops you, skip it: we'll work on it together in the studio.

title: You, in the
story
modules.why: Small brands start with someone. We want the story, not the CV.

items.label: Why now?
items.help: What changed that made you start this brand?
items.placeholder: Write it the way you'd say it over coffee.
suggestions: We saw a problem nobody was solving
Our clients asked for it
It was time to do things properly
We grew and the old brand no longer fits

items.label: A real story where your brand mattered to someone.
items.help: It could become the brand story, so keep the small details.
items.placeholder: There was this one day when…
suggestions: It was an ordinary day until
A client wrote to us after
The nicest compliment we ever got
The first time we felt we'd made a difference

items.label: How visible do you want to be in the brand?

pairs.right: Company brand, me in the background

items.label: What do people do better after they've met you?
items.placeholder: One thing, as concrete as you can.
suggestions: They choose more easily
They have more time
They feel more confident
They understand what they're buying

title: Your
people
modules.why: Your first clients decide what the brand looks like to everyone else. Let's see their faces.

items.label: Who are your first clients? Sketch 2 or 3 profiles.
items.help: Think of real people. Just change their names.

fields.label: What frustrates them today
fields.placeholder: What doesn't work with the options they have now

items.label: Who do you turn away?
items.help: Up to 3. A clear brand also knows who it isn't for.

options.label: People after the lowest price, no matter what
People who want it all in 48 hours
People who want the standard version everyone else has
People who want to control every detail

items.label: Drag the steps into the order they matter to your typical client.
items.help: The top is what matters most.

title: Your place
on the map
modules.why: Positioning is the place you hold in someone's mind. If you don't pick it, the market picks it for you.

items.label: How do you explain your brand to someone over coffee, in 10 seconds?

options.label: The version that says what it does.
The version that says who it's for.
The version that says why it's different.

items.label: What do people use today instead of you?
items.help: For each one: what it does well and where it falls short.

rows.label: The big player in the category

items.label: X factor: what can you promise that nobody else can?
items.help: Just one thing. If a competitor can say it too, it's not the one.
suggestions: We're the only ones who
We always pick up the phone
We make everything by hand
Results guaranteed or your money back

items.label: Drag each slider to where you stand today.

title: If it were
a person
modules.why: If the brand were a person, how would you spot them from across the room? There's no right answer, only an honest one.

items.label: Drag each slider toward the word that fits better.
If the brand walked into a room full of people, how would it act?
items.placeholder: It would be the one who…
suggestions: It would introduce itself to everyone
It would listen more than it talks
It would crack the joke that breaks the ice
It would know the answer to any question

title: Values
modules.why: Values are promises you keep even when they cost you. We pick them by elimination, so only the true ones are left.

items.label: Eight, then five, then three.
items.help: Drag the values into the basket. You can add one of your own.

title: What you give,
what they feel
modules.why: Rational attributes say what people get. Emotional ones say what they're left with. We need both.

items.label: Three rational attributes. What does the brand offer?
Three emotional attributes. How do people feel?
What do you want someone to say about the brand after the first meeting?
suggestions: I've never met anyone who
They really care
Simple, no hassle
They know exactly what they're doing

title: Voice
modules.why: Voice is how you sound when you're not in the room. Go with your gut. Don't overthink it.

items.label: An offer. Which one sounds like your brand?

a.label: Complete package, 5-day delivery, 2-year warranty. Order now.

b.label: It arrives on Friday, ready to use. If something isn't right, we come and fix it.

items.label: A welcome message.

a.label: Welcome! Thank you for signing up. You will receive updates soon.

b.label: Hi, Anna. Glad you're here. On Thursday we're hosting an evening for new clients, 12 seats. Shall we save you one?

items.label: Someone asks “how much is it?”

a.label: Rates start from 200 lei, as per our price list.

b.label: Straight answer: 200 lei. And the first coffee's on us.

items.label: Us, not us. Drag each word into its basket.
items.help: Three words the brand uses and three it would never use.

items.label: How formal is the brand?

options.label: First names, always
options.desc: In contracts and on Instagram alike.

options.label: First names, with exceptions
options.desc: Formal in paperwork and with people who prefer it.

options.label: Depends on the channel
options.desc: Casual on social, formal on the website and in email.

title: How it
looks
modules.why: No stock photos. Just colors, type, textures and rhythm, so you pick the feeling, not the cliché.

items.label: In each pair, which one feels closer?
Got references of your own? Up to six.
items.help: Images or links, from any field. Tell us what you like about each one.

items.label: What should it NOT look like?

title: The website
and the rest
modules.why: Your first website doesn't have to do everything. It has to do three things well in its first three months.

items.label: What does the website need to do in its first 3 months? Put it in order.
Domain and social accounts you already own
Deadlines: when does it need to be ready?
suggestions: Launch in 3 months
Before the autumn season
No rush, we want it right
We have an event on

items.label: What does success look like in 6 months? Three numbers to watch.

agenda.title: Coffee and ground rules
agenda.goal: What we do today and what we leave with: The Core, the archetype mix and the profiles.

agenda.title: The foundation
agenda.goal: What we keep from what you've already said. How much of the brand is you.

agenda.title: People and positioning
agenda.goal: First clients, who we turn away, the positioning sentence and the X factor.

agenda.title: Personality and archetype
agenda.goal: Two archetypes and a percentage. The referee for design decisions.

agenda.title: Values and attributes
agenda.goal: We vote. Three values with “always / never”, attributes 3 + 3.

agenda.title: Voice and visuals
agenda.goal: How it sounds and how it feels. What we avoid at all costs.

agenda.title: Architecture and website
agenda.goal: The order of priorities, the sub-brand calls, what the site does in 3 months.

agenda.title: Writing The Core
agenda.goal: One sentence. What you offer, to whom, in what culture, in what voice, what it gives them, how they feel.

core.label: In what culture
core.hint: the place, the pace, the values

core.label: In what voice
core.hint: three words for how you sound

core.label: X factor
core.hint: what you promise and others can't

done.title: Prep done. See you in the studio.
done.body: We have everything. We'll read it before we meet, and when we start working you'll find your answers already in The Core, right where they belong. The rest we do together, over a coffee, at Olari 9.
